Subject: ACME RAG eval — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Great discussion — wanted to capture the key takeaways and a proposed plan so we’re aligned. TL;DR: we think a hybrid dense-retriever + small cross-encoder reranker gives the best tradeoff for your QA workflow given latency and budget targets.

Recap / Goals:
- Primary UX: instant-like answers for internal docs + policy pages (target P95 latency <= 800ms).
- Quality thresholds: Grounding Rate >= 92% (answers that cite / are supported by a doc), Hallucination Rate <= 3% on our 500-sample prompt set.
- Scale: ~120k queries/month; median doc size ~10k tokens, expect frequent long-context retrievals.

Recommended baseline (what we propose to evaluate first):
1) Retriever: dense FAISS index with 1k-token chunks, embeddings via redwood/embedding-small. Retrieval top_k = 12.
2) Reranker: cross-encoder (reranker-large) applied to top 12 -> re-rank to top 3. This yields best grounding precision in our benchmarks; see attached summary.
3) Generator: redwood/llama-2-13b-q4 for high-quality grounding + cost control. We can test a smaller 7B variant if budget becomes a hard constraint.
4) Caching/prefixing: enable prefix KV caching for repeated conversational sessions to reduce token cost by ~20%.

Metrics & benchmarks referenced:
- R-Precision, MRR@5, Grounding Rate (we define as percent of answers that include at least one correct doc passage), and Hallucination Rate. See: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/rag-grounding-metrics
- Attached: redwood-rag-eval-summary.pdf (short results + retrieval/reranker tradeoffs)

Immediate next steps (asks from ACME):
- Share a 1-2GB sample of red-teamed docs (we can accept an S3 link or Drive). We’ll index a subset and run the first pass of evaluators.
- Approve a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive next week to validate latency envelope and reranker latency (Rishi + Neha propose Wed/Thu).
- Confirm whether you want a heavy-reranker-only path (best quality, higher cost) vs hybrid (recommended).

I’ve attached our high-level evaluation summary and included the prompt set we used internally (acme-prompt-set.csv). If that works, I’ll kick off the indexing job once we have sample data and lock the deep-dive time.

Thanks —
Marissa

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we share data:
1) Reranker latency: our SLO for interactive search is 700ms P95. How much additional latency does reranker-large add if used on top 12?
2) Cost: can you ballpark cost differential between heavy reranker-only vs hybrid approach at our projected 120k queries/mo?

We’re leaning hybrid but want concrete numbers. Also, can you confirm what minimal anonymization is acceptable for the sample dataset? We’ll strip PII but want to make sure it’s usable for retrieval tests.

Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval — post-call recap & next steps

Samir —

Great Qs, answered inline below.

1) Reranker latency: reranker-large (cross-encoder) adds ~120-220ms per candidate on modern GPUs; doing it on top 12 typically adds 150-200ms end-to-end if run in a single batch. With our optimized batching and cross-encoder kernels we’ve seen median +160ms. Hybrid pattern (score top 12 with a cheap bi-encoder and only rerank top 6) brings that number closer to +80-110ms. We can run a latency-focused test during the deep-dive to validate.

2) Cost: rough estimates for 120k queries/mo (back-of-envelope):
- Heavy reranker-only (rerank all candidates with reranker-large): ~ $X,XXX/mo incremental compute (higher GPU cycles), higher token cost for generator due to different reranking precision.
- Hybrid (dense retriever + reranker on top N=6): ~ 35-45% lower incremental compute cost vs reranker-only while keeping ~98% of quality gains.
We’ll provide a line-item estimate in the follow-up doc for procurement.

3) Data anonymization: stripping PII (names, emails) and keeping document structure/sections is fine — we still need realistic paragraph boundaries and any tables in context. S3 link or Drive with ACL to redwood-eval@redwood.ai works. We’ll treat the data under our standard NDA — if you want, we can sign a short addendum covering data retention for the eval.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Rishi/Neha: schedule the technical deep-dive Wed/Thu PST.
- I’ll prepare a short cost worksheet and two latency profiles (reranker-only and hybrid) and drop in the Drive folder before the deep-dive.

If that all sounds good I can send a calendar invite and a quick PRD for the eval.

Best,
Marissa
